nodes.label: Planning the set on the beat
nodes.rationale: Songs are laid out in the playlist's order, on the beat of the one playing, on a 16-bar phrase before its outro (from each song's sound profile). The next song comes in so its drop lands where the bass changes hands, so the playing song is never left without its bass while the next is still in its intro.

nodes.label: Drop detection from the bassline
nodes.rationale: A drop is where a song's bassline comes in: a kick alone falls away between the beats, a bassline holds the lows up. Read from the waveform, or from loudness when there is none; the bass change is placed on it.

nodes.label: Mixing styles (one at a time, continuous, double drops)
nodes.rationale: One at a time is an 8-bar blend; Continuous uses 32-bar blends with a bass swap (shorter for short songs); Double drops land the next song's first drop on a drop of the playing one when tempos are within 6 % and keys fit, else a bass swap. Tempos more than 8 % apart are cut on the phrase instead.

nodes.label: Decks: 2 or 3 lanes and layering
nodes.rationale: Songs take turns across 2 or 3 lanes. On 3 decks, two similar songs in a row (close tempos, fitting keys) are layered: the second comes in early and plays with the first for 48 bars, then the next comes in before the first goes, three at once for 16 bars. Only one has its bass at a time.

nodes.label: Length to fit
nodes.rationale: No limit, or 30 minutes to 3 hours: every song plays a little shorter (an earlier phrase); if that is not enough, the last songs are left out.

nodes.label: The timeline
nodes.rationale: Each song is drawn where it plays, as heard: its waveform shrinks as it fades and loses its lows while its bass is cut, over a faint copy of the song as it is. A faint bar grid lines things up. The play button and timeline stay at the top while the running order scrolls.

nodes.label: Hand-overs
nodes.rationale: Each hand-over has a chip under the lanes; its box sets the style (Blend, Bass swap, Layer, Filter sweep, Echo out, Cut, Double drop), whose bass plays (Auto, Outgoing, Incoming, Both), length, the next song earlier or later, how alike the two sound, and Hear it. An orange bass marker on the timeline shows where the bass changes hands.

nodes.label: Bass cut or opened by hand
nodes.rationale: Hovering a song shows a bass strip along its foot that grows under the pointer; dragging along it cuts the song's bass over those bars or opens it where it was cut. Cut stretches are hatched red, opened ones orange, each with an x to let go.

nodes.label: Listening through GLUE Home
nodes.rationale: With GLUE Home 0.84 or later running, it reads the songs from disk, mixes them and streams the mix to the page (Mixed by GLUE Home); nothing is copied into the browser. If a song is not on that computer, the browser mixes instead. Play uses the same mixer as the exported file.

nodes.label: The running order
nodes.rationale: Dragging a song changes the playlist's order and the set is planned again (Undo brings back the one before). The song playing fills its line as it goes; clicking a song's name opens its menu on the timeline.

nodes.label: Exporting the mix
nodes.rationale: WAV 24-bit 44.1 kHz or MP3 320, mixed song by song in the background; a part of the set can be chosen by its first and last song; the tracklist with times opens in its own window.
